name: Saskell Creek Early Learning Center
programs: Half-day and full-day PreK|Speech and language screening|Family literacy nights
summary: Half-day and full-day PreK for three- and four-year-olds, with developmental screening and family literacy nights.
body:
The Early Learning Center serves every neighborhood in the district. Children who turn four by September 1 (story) are eligible for full-day PreK; three-year-olds attend half days.

Screenings for speech, hearing and vision happen in the first six weeks, and families get a written summary.

name: Ostby Elementary
programs: Outdoor classroom|Before- and after-school care|Reading intervention
summary: A K–5 school at the top of the Ridge line, with an outdoor classroom on the creek bank.
body:
Ostby is the district's oldest building still in use (story: 1931), renovated in 2019 with a new library and an accessible entrance on Ostby Road.

Students walk to the outdoor classroom twice a week for science and writing.

name: Fernhall Elementary
summary: A K–5 school with a Spanish–English dual-language strand from kindergarten.
body:
Half of each grade at Fernhall learns in Spanish and English from kindergarten, with the goal of biliteracy by fifth grade. Families choose the strand in the spring before kindergarten.

The robotics club meets Tuesdays and Thursdays after school in the library.

name: Marrow Street Elementary
programs: Music and art every week|Gifted cluster classrooms|Garden club
summary: A K–5 school near downtown, with music and art every week in every grade.
body: Marrow Street students have music and art each week from kindergarten, and the fifth grade puts on a spring musical in the Saskell Ridge High auditorium.

name: Juno Park Middle School
programs: Algebra I in grade 8|Band, orchestra and choir|Spanish continuation for dual-language students
summary: Grades 6–8 for the Ridge line. Every Fernhall dual-language student can continue Spanish here.
body: Juno Park runs on a six-period day with an advisory period every morning. Students who finish Math 7 Accelerated take Algebra I in grade 8 for high school credit.

name: Saskell Ridge High School
programs: Advanced Placement (14 courses)|Theater and auditorium|Dual credit with the community college
summary: The Ridge line's high school: 14 Advanced Placement courses, a 600-seat auditorium and dual credit with the community college.
body: Saskell Ridge offers fourteen AP courses and dual-credit English and history taught on campus. The auditorium hosts the district's winter and spring concerts.

name: Bramble Lane Elementary
summary: A neighborhood K–5 at the start of the Creek line, with free breakfast for every student.
body: Breakfast is served in classrooms from 7:40 am, free for every student (story: community eligibility).

name: Quarry Hill Elementary
status_note: Two-hour delay today: boiler repair. Breakfast at 9:40.
programs: STEM lab|Special education resource center|Before- and after-school care
summary: A K–5 with a STEM lab and the district's elementary special education resource center.
body: Quarry Hill hosts the district resource center for students with significant support needs in grades K–5, with sensory spaces and a fully accessible playground.

name: Tillet Elementary
programs: English learner newcomer center|Family resource room|Garden club
summary: A K–5 with the district's newcomer center for English learners and a family resource room.
body: Families new to the country start at Tillet's newcomer center, with interpreters in Spanish, Arabic, Vietnamese and Dari (story) and a family resource room open every morning.

name: Lantern Bridge Middle School
summary: Grades 6–8 for the Creek line, with project-based science and a robotics team.
body: Lantern Bridge runs a project-based science program: each grade spends six weeks on a creek-restoration study with the county conservation district (story).

name: Saskell Creek High School
programs: International Baccalaureate diploma|Marching band|Stadium and natatorium
summary: The Creek line's high school: the IB diploma programme, the district stadium and the natatorium.
body: Saskell Creek High offers the IB diploma programme alongside a full course catalog. The district stadium and pool are on this campus.

name: Old Mill Elementary
status_note: Early release today: family conferences from 1:15 pm.
summary: A K–5 in the mill district with a Montessori-inspired primary program.
body: Kindergarten through second grade at Old Mill use mixed-age classrooms and hands-on materials; grades 3–5 follow the district curriculum.

name: Weaver Street Elementary
status_note: Early release today: family conferences from 1:15 pm.
programs: Spanish–English dual language|Choir|Before- and after-school care
summary: A K–5 with the Mill line's dual-language strand and a choir that sings at every board meeting in December.
body: Weaver Street opened its dual-language strand in 2022 (story), and adds a grade each year.

name: Millrace Middle School
programs: Industrial tech and makerspace|Algebra I in grade 8|Orchestra
summary: Grades 6–8 for the Mill line, with a makerspace in the old weaving shed.
body: Millrace's makerspace sits in the restored weaving shed: laser cutters, a wood shop and a recording booth.

name: Kestle Mill High School
summary: The Mill line's high school, with an early-college pathway and an agriculture program with its own barn.
body: Students in the early-college pathway can graduate with an associate degree from the community college (story) at no cost to families.

name: Northgate Career and Technical Center
programs: Health sciences|Welding and manufacturing|Culinary arts|IT and cybersecurity
summary: A half-day career center shared by all three high schools: health sciences, welding, culinary arts and IT.
body:
Juniors and seniors from all three high schools spend half of each day at Northgate. Buses run from each high school at 7:35 am and 11:50 am.

Programs lead to industry certifications (story): CNA, AWS welding, ServSafe and CompTIA A+.
